answer: Sybil resistance can be priced in sequential time. To register, an agent must finish a verifiable delay function, a hash chain whose length sets a minimum wall-clock cost no parallel hardware can compress. One identity per completed chain, so a thousand clones queue for a thousand chains: a slow voyage, not a cheap batch. Seeds come from a public beacon, so precomputation is useless, and the fastest falcon in a cluster gains no edge over a laptop. Each finished chain is filed as an opal, a one-use token three independent nodes recheck before the seat opens; a forgery breaks the chain at once.
